basis: Defective, hypoplastic pulmonary alveolar development defines the disease; the cardiac ancestry does not establish heart involvement.
Muscular dystrophy, early contractures and cardiac disease form the defining clinical triad; cardiac involvement qualifies by diagnostic importance.
Diffuse pancreatic beta-cell dysfunction causes uncontrolled insulin secretion and hypoglycemia; neurological injury is not established as common.
Dermal histiocytic aggregates cause persistent cutaneous papules; the definition explicitly excludes mucosal and visceral involvement.
Neoplasm directly involving the vagus nerve.
Primary skeletal dysplasia; conductive hearing loss is common across major spectrum disorders, approximately >=30%; cleft palate is subtype-dependent.
Progressive CNS degeneration with neuronal loss in 20/20 patients; gaze palsy and eyelid apraxia reflect central neurological dysfunction.
Inherited cardiac electrical dysfunction causing ventricular arrhythmias; abnormal calcium handling does not establish a systemic metabolic disorder.
Congenital structural and valvular heart disease defines the condition; extracardiac findings are variable without established common organ damage.
Inherited retinal degeneration caused by biallelic RAB28 variants.
Endocrine pancreatic islet proliferation and insulin dysregulation; cataract and glaucoma each occur in 4/24, below 30%.
Striatal disease causes dystonia, ataxia and motor disability; dysphagia and oculomotor apraxia reflect neurological dysfunction.
Skeletal muscle chloride channelopathy causes myotonia, stiffness and weakness; no independent nerve or CNS disease is established.
Combined cellular and humoral immunodeficiency; secondary infections are separate diseases and organ damage varies across this umbrella.
Gonococcal infection of the prostate; prostate has no anatomical axis, but the infectious mechanism qualifies.
Autosomal recessive PROM1-related retinal disease.
Auditory canal malformation with hearing impairment in 6/6; persistent ptosis affects eyelids in 3/4 (75%); microphthalmos alone is below threshold.
Parathyroid carcinoma; hormone-mediated bone loss occurs in 30-79%. Kidney stones are separate disease; renal insufficiency is 5-29%; deposits alone do not prove dysfunction.
Hereditary colorectal cancer susceptibility defines a gastrointestinal target; predisposition alone does not establish existing cancer or organ damage.
Carcinoma arising in breast tissue, which is outside the 13 axes.
Broad chromosome 15 disorder umbrella; neurodevelopmental impairment is characteristic across the listed major subtypes; other organ abnormalities vary.
Carcinoma arising in a major salivary gland, usually the parotid; salivary glands belong to the gastrointestinal axis.
Disease directly involving the ciliary body; the umbrella includes inflammatory and neoplastic conditions without a shared immune mechanism.
Inherited epidermal fragility with intraepidermal blistering in 9/9 patients; no common extracutaneous damage is established.
Tumour arises in eyelid epidermis; its defining location is both skin and eyelid, which are explicitly covered by these axes.
